sentences.text: Shri Sameer Verma, learned counsel for the appellant.
Ms. Preeti Saxena, learned counsel for respondent no.3  ORDER

This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 24.03.2018 passed by Member, MACT, Indore in Claim Case No.170/2012 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
in case of injury suffered by the claimant, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,27,500/- alongwith interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization in favour of the claimant.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
He further submitted that the Tribunal has erred in assessing the income of the claimant as Rs.3,000/-.

However, accepting the earning of the claimant as Rs.3,500/-
per month and adding future prospects adequate and reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded in the case.

The amount awarded under the head of pain and suffering, loss of wages are on Rajendra vs Bhagwan on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196961326/
1
lower side and no amount has been awarded under the head of attendant, hence, prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the matter.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.
5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side which deserves to be enhanced as under:
Permanent Disability Rs.3,500/- x 12 =Rs.42,000/-
 plus Rs.16,
 =Rs.58,800/- x  =Rs.2,64,600/-
 Total Compensation Rs.2,64,600/- 
 MACT awarded Rs.1,62,000/-=
6.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case in regard to permanent disability is Rs.2,64,600/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.1,02,600/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
7. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed to the extent indicated herein above.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
